title: fix: close the 1.28.0 carry-overs and the guard holes found
headline: The 1.28.0 carry-overs close here, with the guard holes found on the way: a protected file under another Windows name, a write into `.git` by move or copy, and a push carried to another host. The rule text planned for this build did not pass the recall bar and is not in it.
alignment: v1.29.0 is the minor release build 3 plans, less its rule text: the recall gate refused it and the gate was not lowered.

items.text: A protected file named with dots or spaces on its end (`settings.json.`) or a stream suffix (`guard.cjs::$DATA`) is read as the file Windows opens. On 1.28.0 PowerShell could write the settings or a guard that way with no hold.
items.where: A protected file under another Windows name
items.after: Held as the file it opens

items.text: A move, a copy or an unpack into `.git` itself, its worktrees or `.ssh` is held, as a write to `.git/config` or the hooks always was; so is the config folder under a name of its own.

A device or share spelling of a local path (`\\?\C:\...`, `\\localhost\C$\...`) is read as the local path, and one that cannot be placed is held while a project lists folders. A shell word through a link is read as the file it reaches.

Changing what carries a push (`core.sshCommand`, a proxy, the certificate check, the credential helper) asks for the owner's yes, as changing the URL does. A feature push asks when origin pushes to another repo than it fetches from.
items.where: A feature push after `git config core.sshCommand ...`
items.before: Ran with no yes, to another host

items.text: The folder list `.claude/protected-folders.json` is never written by a tool, and install records it outside the project: gone, changed or not yet recorded, every call is held. The owner accepts a change in their own terminal.
items.where: A branch switch, a reset or one yes that removes the list
items.before: Every listed folder lost its hold
items.after: Every call is held until the owner accepts it

items.text: A PowerShell listing piped into a writer is held when it is recursive with no folder named, uses `-Exclude`, or filters by a pattern that fits a guard file's name, in every form PowerShell takes for the parameter.

In PowerShell a wildcard under plain folders (`tests/*`) is no longer held as a write to a guard when the folder holds no dot name, no link and no kit file at any depth. Only for a one-statement command of plain text.
A project whose path is over 200 characters is found by the session folder name as it is shortened; two such projects alike in their first 200 characters are held, not guessed.

The mutation measure flips only the lines a branch changed and prints the flip count and a rough minute count first. The whole kit runs only when started by hand with scope set to all. A bad base stops the run.
The guard timing tests keep their 8 s limit by the clock on a machine of normal speed. On a machine measured slow the guard's own work is held to 8 s, so a slow runner no longer fails them.

Each of the 25 flipped lines the 1.28.0 measure left alive was built and run: 14 now fail a test, 5 are shown equal by 13,048 compared readings, 6 are equal by what reads them. Three restated test lines were cut on the owner's yes.
The test check names a rule that a change itself adds to the rule index; the link scan, a CI gate with no failing case, has a test; a used pop-up yes is tested not to answer a second ask.

decisions.decision: The rule text is not in this release
decisions.why: Three recall rounds scored it 11 against a bar of 12, and a probe showed the push question passes under half the time on the released kit too. The text was pulled, the bar kept.

decisions.decision: The folder list is recorded by install
decisions.why: A git lookup missed a branch whose last commit did not touch the list and froze a project that removed its list on purpose. A record outside the project covers every way the list can go.

decisions.decision: A program that clears its own markers is a named limit
decisions.why: A check of the push's parent processes was probed: half a second a push, and nothing found for a child started apart from its parent.

verification: Each fix that changes behaviour shipped with a test that fails on the code before it; the review's fixes too (25cc097, e191664, 1127e5e, 1b72c7b, 4378a66).
The Windows name hole was reproduced on disk and against the released 1.28.0 before the fix; both guard proofs and the install check's planted cases pass on this build.
The timing test fails 9 s of work, a 12 s wait and an 8.5 s wait on the owner's PC, and passes the unchanged guard in 1.9 s.

tests.flips: declared tests on main and on this branch; the PR run gives the final count

dimensions.name: Privacy
dimensions.result: One low (a line about the owner's sign-in in the plan), fixed

dimensions.name: Supply chain
dimensions.result: Clean: the workflow's inputs reach steps only as environment values

dimensions.name: Code security
dimensions.result: Five highs fixed; every medium and low fixed or accepted by the owner

dimensions.name: Gaps, scaling, test value
dimensions.result: The timing limit restored to 8 s by the clock; an extra git call per tool call gone with the redesign

dimensions.name: Alignment
dimensions.result: YES; the plan file corrected after the rule text was pulled

fixed: H1: the folder list was found on another branch only when that branch's last commit touched it. Fixed in 25cc097 and e191664.
H2: a move or copy into `.git` landed a config or a hooks folder there. Fixed in e191664.
H3: a device or share spelling of a local path wrote inside a listed folder. Fixed in e191664 and 1127e5e.
H4: a transport setting moved a feature push to another host. Fixed in 1127e5e.
H5: a guard that matched the accept flag's text could be spelled round. Fixed in e191664, in the install itself.
accepted: A PowerShell shell that keeps its own folder between calls, and a race between two calls.
A protected file's name with a full stop after it in prose is held, as the same line without the stop always was.
The Windows name rule runs on macOS and Linux too.
A tool can no longer edit the folder list even with a yes: the K34 change itself.
